source_text:
Fragmenta in epistulam ii ad Thessalonicenses (in catenis)
2 Thess: Prolog
Πάλιν ἐπὶ τοῖς διωγμοῖς οἷς ὑπέμενον οἱ Θεσσαλονικεῖς παραμυθεῖται αὐτούς, ἐξ
αὐτοῦ τοῦ προοιμίου μνημονεύσας τῆς δικαίας καὶ μεγάλης ἀνταποδόσεως τοῦ
Χριστοῦ τῆς τοὺς πονηροὺς ἀμυνομένης, τοὺς δὲ ἁγίους στεφανούσης. εἶτα ἐπειδὴ
πολλὴ ζήτησις ἦν περὶ τῆς δευτέρας τοῦ Χριστοῦ παρουσίας τὸ πότε ἐλεύσεται, καὶ
περὶ τούτου διορθοῦται τὰς ὑπολήψεις, ὥστε μὴ προλαμβάνεσθαι ἢ παραφέρεσθαι
ταῖς ξέναις διδασκαλίαις. ὑποτίθεται καὶ τὸν τρόπον καὶ τὴν ἀκολουθίαν τῆς
παρουσίας Χριστοῦ τῆς πάλιν ἐσομένης μετὰ τὴν τοῦ ἀντιχρίστου πλάνην. 2 Thess
1,3 Ἡ μετὰ δικαιοσύνης ἀγάπη τὸ μὴ μόνον ἀγαπᾶν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀνταγαπᾶσθαι. 2 Thess
1,6®8 Οὐκ ἀμφιβολίας ἐστὶ τὸ εἴπερ δίκαιον, ἀλλ' ἐπιτάσεως καὶ ὁμολογίας· καὶ γὰρ
ἐν ἤθει εἴρηται, ὡς πολλάκις φαμέν, ἡμέρας οὔσης· «εἴπερ ἡμέρα ἔστιν». ∆ιδόντος
ἐκδίκησιν τοῖς μὴ εἰδόσι τὸν θεόν, ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐπάγοντος τιμωρίαν τοῖς ἀσεβοῦσιν.
Μετ' ἀγγέλων δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ ἐν φλογὶ πυρός. τὸ φοβερὸν τῆς ἐνδόξου παρουσίας
παρίστησι καὶ διὰ τούτων, καὶ δι' ὧν ἐπάγει τοὺς ἠδικημένους παραθαρρύνων·
μεγάλη γὰρ παραμυθία οὐ μόνον ὁ μισθὸς ὁ ὑπὲρ τῶν παθῶν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡ κατὰ τῶν
ἠδικηκότων αὐτοὺς γενομένη τιμωρία. 2 Thess 1,10 Ὅτι ἐπιστεύθη τὸ μαρτύριον
ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ· ἡ γὰρ ἐνταῦθα πίστις προευτρεπίζει τὸν μισθὸν ἐν τῇ
ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ. ποίᾳ; ἐν ᾗ ἥξει ὁ Χριστός. 2 Thess 2,1®4 Παραινεῖ αὐτοὺς μὴ
θορυβεῖσθαι ἀκαίρως πρὸ τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ κυρίου, μήτε εἰ προφῆται λέγοιεν εἶναι
ἐν οἷς πνεῦμα πλάνης ἐστίν, μήτε εἰ λόγοι καὶ φῆμαι περὶ τοῦ κυρίου
κατασπείροιντο, μήτε εἰ ἐπιστολήν τινες πλασάμενοι κομίζοιεν ὡς ἡμετέραν. ὅτι ἐὰν
μὴ ἔλθῃ ἡ ἀποστασία πρῶτον καὶ ἀποκαλυφθῇ ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς
ἀπωλείας, ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ 333 ὑπεραιρόμενος ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον θεὸν ἢ
σέβασμα. μὴ προσδοκᾶτε, φησί, τὸν σωτῆρα πρὸ τοῦ πλάνου ὃν δεῖ πρότερον ἐλθεῖν,
καθὼς ἔφην.
thought_title: Paul's comfort and correction for the Thessalonians
orientation: Severian opens his commentary on 2 Thessalonians by summarizing Paul's purpose: to comfort the Thessalonians in persecution and correct their alarm about the timing of Christ's second coming.
pass_a_gloss: Again in the persecutions which the Thessalonians were enduring he comforts them, having remembered from the very prologue the just and great recompense of Christ which punishes the wicked and crowns the saints. Then since there was much inquiry about the second coming of Christ, when he will come, he also corrects their assumptions about this, so that they not be overtaken or carried away by strange teachings. He also sets forth the manner and the sequence of the coming of Christ which will be again after the deception of the antichrist. Love with righteousness is not only to love but also to be loved in return. The 'if indeed it is just' is not of doubt but of emphasis and confession; for it is said as a manner of speaking, as we often say when it is day: 'if indeed it is day.' Giving vengeance to those who do not know God, instead of bringing punishment upon the impious. With the angels of his power in a flame of fire. He presents the terror of the glorious coming both through these things and through the things by which he encourages those who have been wronged; for great comfort is not only the reward for the sufferings but also the punishment that comes upon those who wronged them. Because our testimony was believed in that day; for the faith here prepares the reward in that day. In which day? In which Christ will come. He urges them not to be troubled untimely before the appearing of the Lord, neither if prophets should claim to be among whom a spirit of error is, nor if words and rumors about the Lord should be spread, nor if some should forge a letter and bring it as ours. That unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction, the one who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship. Do not expect, he says, the Savior before the deceiver who must come first, as I said.

choices.why: The glossary does not fix this term, but 'recompense' preserves the reciprocal force of ἀνταπόδοσις (giving back in return) and fits the context of just retribution.
Required by the glossary; 'rebellion' captures the falling away from God that must precede the day of the Lord.
Required by the glossary; the phrase identifies the antichrist figure, and 'lawlessness' renders ἁμαρτία in its Pauline sense of sin as lawlessness.
Required by the glossary; 'coming' renders παρουσία consistently for both Christ's return and the counterfeit coming of Satan.
Required by the glossary; 'appearing' distinguishes ἐπιφάνεια from παρουσία and emphasizes the manifestation of the Lord.
The glossary lists this as a source form for the antichrist but does not fix an English rendering; 'the one who opposes' is literal and preserves the participial force of ἀντικείμενος.

bible_refs.note: εἴπερ δίκαιον ... διδόντος ἐκδίκησιν τοῖς μὴ εἰδόσι τὸν θεόν ... ἐν φλογὶ πυρός
ὅτι ἐπιστεύθη τὸ μαρτύριον ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ
μὴ θροεῖσθαι ... ἐὰν μὴ ἔλθῃ ἡ ἀποστασία πρῶτον καὶ ἀποκαλυφθῇ ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας

pass_b_english: Again Paul comforts the Thessalonians in the persecutions they were enduring, recalling from the very opening of the letter the just and great recompense of Christ, which punishes the wicked and crowns the saints. Then, since there was much debate about the second coming of Christ—when he would come—he corrects their assumptions about this too, so that they would not be overtaken or carried away by strange teachings. He also sets forth the manner and the sequence of Christ's coming, which will take place again after the deception of the antichrist.
Love joined with righteousness means not only loving but also being loved in return (2 Thessalonians 1:3).

The phrase "if indeed it is just" is not an expression of doubt but of emphasis and affirmation. It is said as a manner of speaking, just as we often say when it is daytime, "if indeed it is day." "Giving vengeance to those who do not know God" means bringing punishment upon the ungodly (2 Thessalonians 1:6-8).

"With his mighty angels in flaming fire" (2 Thessalonians 1:7-8). By these words he presents the terror of the glorious coming, and by what he adds he encourages those who have been wronged. For it is a great comfort not only to receive the reward for one's sufferings but also to see punishment come upon those who have wronged them.
"Because our testimony was believed on that day" (2 Thessalonians 1:10). For the faith here prepares the reward beforehand on that day. On what day? The day on which Christ comes.

He urges them not to be alarmed prematurely before the appearing of the Lord—not if those in whom a spirit of error dwells claim to be prophets, not if words and rumors about the Lord are scattered about, not if some forge a letter and bring it as though it were ours (2 Thessalonians 2:1-4).

"Unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction, the one who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship" (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4). Do not expect the Savior, he says, before the deceiver, who must come first, as I told you.

problems.source_quote: τῆς ... ἀνταποδόσεως ... τῆς τοὺς πονηροὺς ἀμυνομένης
problems.why: Greek says the recompense of Christ defends/protects the wicked, not punishes them.

problems.quote: people claim to be prophets in whom a spirit of error dwells
problems.source_quote: εἰ προφῆται λέγοιεν εἶναι ἐν οἷς πνεῦμα πλάνης ἐστίν
problems.why: The Greek says 'if prophets should say [they are prophets] in whom there is a spirit of error'—the English 'people claim to be prophets in whom a spirit of error dwells' changes the construction. The Greek means 'if they say there are prophets in whom a spirit of error is' or 'if prophets are spoken of as existing in whom...' The English 'people claim to be prophets' makes 'people' the subject claiming, but Greek has 'prophets' as subject of λέγοιεν or object of implied speech. Actually re-reading: 'εἰ προφῆται λέγοιεν εἶναι' = 'if prophets are said to be' or 'if they say prophets are'—passive or impersonal. The English 'people claim to be prophets' is wrong: it suggests people claim for themselves, but Greek suggests false prophets are spoken about/claimed to exist.
problems.fix: if prophets are said to exist in whom a spirit of error dwells
problems.ruling: Greek εἰ προφῆται λέγοιεν εἶναι… = ‘if they say there are prophets…’; English ‘people claim to be prophets…’ makes people the prophets, altering meaning.

edits.old: not if people claim to be prophets in whom a spirit of error dwells
edits.new: not if prophets are said to exist in whom a spirit of error dwells

fixed: Changed 'which punishes the wicked' to 'which defends the wicked' because the Greek ἀμυνομένης means 'defends/protects,' not 'punishes.'

Changed 'not if people claim to be prophets in whom a spirit of error dwells' to 'not if prophets are said to exist in whom a spirit of error dwells' because the Greek προφῆται λέγοιεν εἶναι means prophets are said/claimed to exist, not that people claim to be prophets themselves.

problems.why: Middle ἀμυνομένης with an accusative means "punishes" or "avenges itself on," not "defends"; the English reverses the sense of Christ's judgment.

problems.quote: not if prophets are said to exist in whom a spirit of error dwells
problems.why: Active λέγοιεν ("claim") is misread as passive ("are said"), and predicate nominative προφῆται εἶναι ("to be prophets") is misread as existential.
problems.fix: not if those in whom a spirit of error dwells claim to be prophets
problems.ruling: λέγοιεν is active ‘they claim/say’; εἶναι with προφῆται is ‘to be prophets,’ not passive ‘are said to exist’.

problems.quote: It is said as a matter of character
problems.why: In Greek rhetorical exegesis, ἐν ἤθει means "with a rhetorical/ironic tone" or "by way of understatement," not "as a matter of character."
problems.fix: It is said in a rhetorical tone
problems.ruling: ἐν ἤθει here is rhetorical manner (emphasis/idiom), not ‘character’ as moral quality; misleads the εἴπερ point.

edits.old: not if prophets are said to exist in whom a spirit of error dwells
edits.new: not if those in whom a spirit of error dwells claim to be prophets

edits.old: It is said as a matter of character
edits.new: It is said as a manner of speaking

fixed: 'which defends the wicked' fixed to 'which punishes the wicked': source τῆς τοὺς πονηροὺς ἀμυνομένης with accusative means avenges itself on/punishes, not defends.

'not if prophets are said to exist...' fixed to 'not if those in whom... claim to be prophets': source μήτε εἰ προφῆται λέγοιεν εἶναι ἐν οἷς ... is active λέγοιεν with predicate nominative προφῆται εἶναι, not passive/existential.

'as a matter of character' fixed to 'as a manner of speaking': source ἐν ἤθει εἰρηται with ὡς πολλάκις φαμέν means customary idiom, not moral character; phrased naturally to fit 'just as we often say'.

last_rejected.quote: which defends the wicked and crowns the saints
last_rejected.source_quote: τῆς τοὺς πονηροὺς ἀμυνομένης, τοὺς δὲ ἁγίους στεφανούσης
last_rejected.why: ἀμυνομένης means punishes/avenges, not defends; sense reversed
last_rejected.fix: which punishes the wicked and crowns the saints
last_rejected.ruling: Greek ἀμυνομένης = 'defending', not 'punishing'; translation 'defends the wicked' matches source.

last_rejected.quote: Do not expect the Savior, he says, before the deceiver, who must come first, as I told you.
last_rejected.source_quote: μὴ προσδοκᾶτε, φησί, τὸν σωτῆρα πρὸ τοῦ πλάνου ὃν δεῖ πρότερον ἐλθεῖν, καθὼς ἔφην.
last_rejected.why: English hides that 'as I told you' is Paul's self-quotation, not Severian's comment; 'he says' attribution unclear
last_rejected.fix: 'Do not expect the Savior,' he says, 'before the deceiver, who must come first, as I said.'
last_rejected.ruling: Greek φησί and καθὼς ἔφην both are Paul's words; English 'he says' with 'as I told you' still conveys Paul's warning.
